![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14094439/assets/18a6f3e8c2cb509bcdc576a453d0b351caf8193039a8ef9905522be8feabdfac.png)

Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=5+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )$ for $0\le \theta \le \pi $ (shown in blue in the diagram above).
feedback.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=5+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ),$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta ).
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(5+\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta ))^{2}+(5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\theta ))^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{25+10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )+{sin}^{2}⁡(5\theta )+25{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{25+10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )+1+24{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{26+10\operatorname{sin}⁡(5\theta )+24{cos}^{2}⁡(5\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
